findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The line `totpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The original Lithuanian text `Įdiekite FreeOTP arba Google Authenticator savo įrenginyje...` was removed because the sanitizer disallows `` in `totpStep1` (the English source for this key has no HTML). The replacement text should be a proper Lithuanian translation such as `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programų savo mobiliajame telefone:` instead of Italian. All Lithuanian users of the account theme will see an Italian sentence.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The line `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. The original Lithuanian text with `<a>` tags was removed (correctly, because the English `loginTotpStep1` has no HTML), but the replacement is in Italian rather than Lithuanian. All Lithuanian users of the login theme will see an Italian instruction. The corrected text should be a proper Lithuanian translation (compare with the Slovak sibling file `messages_sk.properties`, which uses `Nainštalujte si do mobilu jednu z nasledujúcich aplikácií:` - actual Slovak).

findings.title: Missing English file causes RuntimeException that aborts verification
findings.body: In `verifySafeHtml()`, when the English counterpart file does not exist (e.g. a new locale added without an `_en.properties` base, or a typo in the locale suffix that prevents the regex from matching), the line `throw new RuntimeException("unable to read file " + englishFile, e)` is thrown. This is wrapped by no try/catch in `verify()`, so it propagates out of the verifier and aborts the whole Maven plugin run for any file that lacks an English counterpart, instead of gracefully skipping the HTML check (or emitting a non-fatal warning). At minimum a `MissingResourceException`/missing file should be turned into a skipped-or-warned result, not a fatal `RuntimeException`.

findings.title: Locale regex character class does not include digits
findings.body: The English-file lookup uses `.replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")`. The character class `[a-zA-Z-_]` excludes digits, so any locale code containing digits (e.g. `pt_BR_abc123` style variants, or future locale extensions) would not be matched and the English path would be computed incorrectly (likely left as the original locale suffix), causing the RuntimeException described above. The class should be `[a-zA-Z0-9-_]` to be robust against any locale suffix.

findings.title: `<!-- -->` strip assumes a specific sanitizer output format
findings.body: `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")` assumes the OWASP sanitizer inserts exactly the literal `<!-- -->` to escape stray braces (e.g. `{<!-- -->0}`). However, depending on the sanitizer version and the surrounding context, the inserted comment may not be exactly that literal (it can contain attributes or differ in whitespace, and the OWASP sanitizer in some versions emits nothing or emits different placeholders). Removing only that exact string and then comparing with `Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` makes the equality check fragile: legitimate curly-brace substitutions may be left as raw HTML-looking text in the comparison, and conversely the strip may be a no-op when it should not be. This should at least be guarded by checking the actual OWASP version's behavior, or the comment should be removed from the code path if no longer produced. Additionally the unescape step `org.apache.commons.text.StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4` (deprecated in commons-text 1.x in favor of `escapeHtml4`/`unescapeHtml4`) is being applied even when the sanitizer did not produce HTML entities for this value, which can mask real diffs.

findings.title: No test for missing English counterpart file
findings.body: The test class only adds fixtures that always have a paired `*_en.properties` (illegalHtmlTag, noHtml, changedAnchor). There is no test that covers the realistic case where a translated file has no English counterpart (e.g. adding a new locale without `messages_en.properties`). Without such a test the `throw new RuntimeException` branch is uncovered and will surface for the first time as a build-breaking failure in production usage.
